judgment.reason: The premises about Ada's clothing form a logical chain of exclusive-or statements. From p9, Ada wears an amber hat (true). From p27, exactly one of {amber hat, copper card} is true, so copper card is false. From p4, exactly one of {copper card, ivory badge} is true, so ivory badge is true. From p19, exactly one of {ivory badge, violet pin} is true, so violet pin is false. From p29, exactly one of {violet pin, teal card} is true, so teal card is true. This chain is valid in classical logic; each step's conclusion is forced by the previous step and the exclusive-or constraint. The Ben register entries are irrelevant. Proof by contradiction confirms: assuming Ada does not wear a teal card forces ivory badge to be false (by p29 and p19), which forces copper card to be true (by p4), which contradicts p27 and p9.
